title: What a change spots outside its own area goes into that area's note, not a new ticket
description:
## As asked

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour), and JKershaw/simple-dispatcher where its notes say the same.

**What this is for.** Harbour's leftover rule files a follow-up ticket for anything a change spots outside its own area. Each landing mints about 1.4 tickets, and this is one reason the backlog grows when we want it to converge. John: "Good to know, not necessarily for now. Reduces a spiral out, especially on large codebases. Larger sweeps and specific tidy ups outside of tasks can still happen." On Jira, Harbour can't create tickets yet, but area notes live in the repo.

**What we want.** A find outside the change's area becomes a Waiting entry in that area's own note. It becomes a ticket only if it breaks something, blocks work or touches safety. Each item still has one home, never both.

**Done when** the rule says so everywhere Harbour states it, and the next close-out with an outside-area find writes a note, not a ticket, unless the find breaks, blocks or touches safety.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** consolidate the decision this task touches
**Why:** Puts one consequence gate under every route that files an outside find, leftover, review's outside marking, ledger settlement, triage and the after-merge audit, and moves note writing before merge; editing the leftover rule alone leaves most minting untouched.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

*Planned at LinearViewer* `94893cc35`*, simple-dispatcher* `a42456c`*. Builds on Survey open-0, Survey global and the Unblock comment (12 Nov), each re-checked against HEAD below.*

### What this is for, and done

Today every stage that spots something outside its own work turns it into a ticket. That mints about 1.4 tickets per landing, and the backlog grows when it should converge. After this change, a find outside the change's area goes into that area's note as a Waiting entry. It becomes a ticket only when it breaks something, blocks work or touches safety. Each find has one home.

**Done when** (the ticket's own words): "the rule says so everywhere Harbour states it, and the next close-out with an outside-area find writes a note, not a ticket, unless the find breaks, blocks or touches safety."

**Cuts to the** `## As asked` **block:** none. The after-merge audit is in scope (Unblock comment, `gate-notes-pr`).

**Drift between the ask and its purpose.** The ask names "Harbour's leftover rule". At HEAD, that rule (`LEFTOVER_RULE`, `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`) is one of four routes that file tickets, and it is not the busiest. Most minting comes from review's outside marking of class siblings and ledger items, close-out's "**Outside**: file it as a follow-up" bullet, and the audit's "file a follow-up ticket … for each finding that still matters". Editing only the constant would look done and barely move the 1.4. This plan puts one gate under all four routes.

### The behaviour, named so its places can be recognised

An **outside find** is anything a stage notices that is not this ticket's own work. It comes in five forms:

* a leftover outside the change's area;
* a class sibling that review marks outside;
* an outside item in the What-CI-Did-Not-Prove ledger;
* something close-out notices for itself;
* an audit finding.

Its **home** is decided once:

* **A ticket**, only if the find *breaks* something (behaviour is wrong today), *blocks* work (a task cannot go ahead without it), or *touches safety* (authentication, secrets, data loss, irreversible writes). Where the provider cannot create tickets (Jira), the find goes to the person in the summary comment instead.
* **Otherwise, a Waiting entry** in the note of the area its first cited file maps to (`docs/areas/areas.json`, first match wins). An unmapped file (`tests/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `.github/`) uses the note of the area whose code it concerns. If it concerns no area's code, or the repo has no area notes, the find goes in the change's summary comment, addressed to the person, and nothing is minted.
* **Never both.**

Any place in the code or docs that tells an agent to *file* an outside find without this test is a place of this behaviour.

### Decisions

**D1. One shared gate:** `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` **in the leaf** `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`**, beside** `LEFTOVER_RULE`**.** It states the home rule above in one string: the three consequences with safety's four named kinds, the provider fallback, and the unmapped and no-notes fallbacks.

* Each route renders it verbatim, once per prompt, and adds only its own sentence about what that actor does.
* It lives in the leaf because the leaf imports nothing (lesson below). The fallback wording is taken from the Periodical rule already in code (`areaNotesRoutes`, `lib/periodicals.js`) rather than invented.
* Set aside: a gate in each template, which gives three spellings that `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js` exists to stop. Also set aside: putting the gate inside `LEFTOVER_RULE`, because leftovers are not defects (D2).

**D2. Leftovers never become tickets.** `LEFTOVER_RULE`'s outside clause changes from "a follow-up only close-out files" to "a Waiting entry in that area's note", with the fallbacks taken from `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`.

* A leftover is, by the rule's own definition, "code shape … not a defect". A leftover that breaks, blocks or touches safety is a defect, and "a defect goes the usual way", which is now the gate.
* The leftover step (`leftoverPrompt`, `lib/dispatch-leftover.js`) writes outside-area entries itself on the PR branch, in the other area's note. It already writes notes there. "List outside items for close-out" becomes "list for close-out only a defect the gate sends to a ticket", and "File nothing yourself" stays.
* This removes a hand-off rather than moving it.

**D3. Who writes, and when.**

* **Review** names a home for each outside find: an area slug with the entry worded as it should land, or "ticket" with which consequence applies and why.
* **Close-out** writes every named entry, including entries in other areas' notes, in **Make the Fixes Review Asked For**, on the PR branch, before the merge. It then re-establishes CI, as it already does for review's own-area entries. `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` runs in CI, so a malformed entry holds the merge instead of landing.
* **Tickets** the gate calls for are still filed in **Follow-up Triage** after the merge. A ticket needs no branch, so moving filing earlier would buy nothing.
* **Settle the Ledger's Outside bullet** settles an outside item one of two ways: by the note commit (cited), or by the gate's ticket, filed in Triage.
* Set aside: moving all of Triage before the merge, which changes more than the problem needs.

**D4. The two axes stay separate.** *Inside or outside the ticket's bounded classes* is scope, and it is discharged by doing or dropping, never by filing (John Kershaw's ruling on LIN-2825). It does not change. The gate only splits the *outside* set.

* Wherever a ruling's options are listed, "file" is offered only for an outside item that passes the gate. Those places are review's scope paragraph, close-out's Triage, and the manual's ruling-options paragraph (`docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md`).

**D5. The after-merge audit follows the Periodical notes path (Unblock comment).** This is a separate piece; see Landing.

* `retrospective-audit` renders `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`. Gate finds become tickets. Every other finding goes as a Waiting entry into **one docs-only PR**, kept green under the notes guard and the required checks, and linked from the audit's comment. An audit with no note-bound findings opens no PR. Its claims and test-integrity checks are unchanged.
* **What this needs that the Periodical path does not.** A Periodical's task stays In Progress, but the audited ticket is already Done. Three things must hold on a Done ticket.
  * **(a) The selector must not pick the audit again while its notes PR is open.** The trail facts already show "Work reported after it: yes", because an agent comment with a PR link counts as landing evidence (`isLandingEvidence`, `lib/recommendation-facts.js`). So the audit's `route.whenNot` gains one clause: a PR linked after the audit and not yet merged goes to `review`, then `close-out`.
  * **(b) Review judges that PR against the audit's findings comment, not the original** `## As asked` **block.** The ask was met at the first merge, and judging a notes PR against it would end in Needs Discussion.
  * **(c) On a ticket already Done, close-out merges the notes PR and posts its summary, and nothing else.** Done, archive and prune, and related tickets were handled at the first close-out.
* Each is one sentence in the template that owns it. Set aside: having the audit reopen the ticket, which corrupts Done-time metrics and contradicts "do not change status". Also set aside: a person merging by hand, which leaves a chore with no owner.
* The route edit changes the selector's prompt, so `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt`, the router snapshots and the routing ceiling move with it (lesson below).

**D6. Periodicals are unchanged.** Their readings are not "a change", so they have no area of their own to be outside of. They already route finds to notes, and urgent breakage to the person and never to a ticket (`routeObjectiveBreakage`, `areaNotesRoutes`, LIN-4379/4380/4349). That is a narrower rule decided on its own ticket, and it is consistent with this one.

**D7. No code guard on ticket creation.** Whether a find breaks, blocks or touches safety is a judgement that code cannot check. All filing is driven by prompts: the only ticket-creating code (`routes/proxy-writes.js`, `routes/task-create.js` and the like) consists of generic write surfaces that people use too.

* The shape is held by tests: D1's constant, the retype guard and a phrase scan over every rendered prompt.
* The production witness is `scripts/follow-on-ratio.mjs` (`lib/follow-on-ratio.js`), which measures tickets filed per done task. Expected direction: down.

### Places

**Piece A: the pre-merge gate (LinearViewer unless noted)**

| Place | Change |
| -- | -- |
| `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` | Add `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`. Rewrite `LEFTOVER_RULE`'s outside clause (D2). Update the header comment to name both constants and their readers. |
| `lib/dispatch-leftover.js` (`leftoverPrompt`) | Render `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`. Outside leftovers are written to the other area's note by the builder. "For close-out" means gate tickets only. |
| `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, review | **Isolated, or One of a Class?**: the leftover read keeps `LEFTOVER_RULE`. **Inside or Outside the Ticket's Scope**: replace "close-out files it, after checking it does not already exist" with "review names its home under `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`" (rendered here once). **What CI Did Not Prove**: replace "an **outside** item … by a routed follow-up ticket" and "it stays an outside-scope follow-up" with the gate's home. **Hand Off to Close-Out**: "file follow-ups" becomes "file the gate's tickets". |
| `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, close-out | Workflow line 2 covers note entries in any area. Line 5's "file the outside follow-ups" becomes the gate's tickets. **Make the Fixes**: write every named entry, own area or other, before the merge. **Settle the Ledger** Outside bullet (D3). **Land It**: the closing sentence's filing clause. **Follow-up Triage**: files only gate tickets. The existing-ticket check, priority and label bullets stay. The `description` field: "file remaining follow-ups" becomes the gate's tickets. |
| `lib/completion-signals.js`, close-out | `coreOutcome`, signal 3 ("an outside item filed on its own terms"), signal 6 ("remaining outside follow-ups filed and linked") and `readinessCheck` ("followed-up") all speak in the gate's terms: a note written before the merge, or a gate ticket filed. |
| `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` | "files the outside follow-ups" in the finish-line paragraph. |
| `docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md` | The ruling-options paragraph ("offer **file** only for a finding outside every bounded class"), and the close-out paragraph's "Only an item **outside** every bounded class … may be filed": add the gate. |
| `docs/areas/README.md` | "Who writes here": retire "Close-out is the only one that files a follow-up". The leftover step and close-out write entries in other areas' notes, and the gate decides tickets. "One home": point at both constants. The exit route "a follow-up is filed for it" stays true: an entry that later breaks, blocks or touches safety becomes a ticket and leaves the note. |
| `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md` (the "What reads the answer" bullet) and `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` (the LIN-4374 paragraph and the review→close-out paragraph) | Say where an outside find goes now. |
| simple-dispatcher `docs/areas/README.md` ("One home for each leftover") | Name `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` beside `LEFTOVER_RULE`, as Harbour's rule rendered into every prompt that routes an outside find. It already restates nothing else, so this is one sentence and a separate PR in that repository. |
| `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` | One row per landed piece. Path: `template`. Expected direction: down (fewer follow-on tickets). |
| `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` | Re-measured ceilings (see Budget). |
| `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js` | `RULE_PIECES` swaps "a follow-up only close-out files" for the new outside clause and adds `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`'s distinctive pieces. The Triage assertion "Only outside items are filed here" changes with the wording. |

**Piece B: the audit (D5)**

`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, in three places:

* `retrospective-audit`: **Reporting**, and its `route.whenNot` clause (a).
* review: sentence (b).
* close-out: sentence (c).

Also:

* `lib/completion-signals.js`, `retrospective-audit` signal 5 ("a follow-up ticket filed for each one that still matters").
* `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt` and the router snapshots (`tests/unit/stage-router-prompt-snapshots.test.js`).
* `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js`'s "post-merge readers are left as they were" block. Retro stays as it was. The audit now carries `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`, but still not the leftover read or "One home for each leftover".

**Out of scope, with reason**

* These are dated records, not live statements of the rule: `docs/papers/**`, `docs/reviews/**`, `docs/plans/**`, `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/*.md` (line-numbered analyses), `scripts/eval/fixtures/**` and `scripts/eval/recommend-baseline/**`, and `scripts/survey-rules-census.mjs` (a census over a frozen JSON snapshot). Rewriting them would falsify their evidence.
* Periodicals: see D6.
* `retro`: it already files nothing ("Do not write them back to Linear"), so there is nothing to change.
* A neglected-area sweep and area mappings for `tests/` and `scripts/` are outside this task (brief, Constraints). Under this very rule they become a Waiting entry, not a ticket. Close-out of piece A writes one into `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, citing `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` first. It says that notes now gather where tickets used to, and that LIN-4414's one retirement per build drains only the areas a build touches, so rarely touched notes (`other-features`) will grow.

**How we know this is every place.** Two checks:

1. A repeatable search, run in both repositories:

   ```
   git grep -n -i -E "follow-up|file it|files it|file the outside|outside item|outside follow" -- lib routes public docs/areas docs/architecture docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md
   ```

   Every hit at `94893cc35` is either in the table above or out of scope with its reason. The hits not listed above are unrelated uses of "follow-up", the session-resume verb: `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, `lib/dispatch-store.js`, `routes/dashboard-rulings.js` and `public/common.js`.
2. The new test below renders **every** stage kind, plus the kickoff and leftover prompts, and fails on any sentence that tells an agent to file an outside find without the gate. A place this search missed, or one written later, goes red there.

### Witnesses (each fails before the change and passes after)

1. **New test** `tests/unit/lin-4401-outside-find-home.test.js`**:**
   * (i) review, close-out and `leftoverPrompt` each contain `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` exactly once, and so does `retrospective-audit` once piece B lands.
   * (ii) `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` names breaks, blocks and safety, with authentication, secrets, data loss and irreversible writes.
   * (iii) no rendered stage prompt, kickoff prompt or close-out/audit completion signal still carries the retired spellings: "a follow-up only close-out files", "**Outside**: file it as a follow-up", "close-out files it, after checking", "file the outside follow-ups", "file a follow-up ticket, readable on its own, for each finding that still matters". The builder settles the exact list from the search.
   * (iv) **The guard's purpose still holds:** close-out's Follow-up Triage still tells close-out to file a gate ticket, so a safety find is not silently routed into a note. This is the test that tries what the old filing was there to stop.
2. **The extended retype guard:** another file under `lib/` or `routes/` that spells a distinctive piece of `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` fails.
3. `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` **stays green** with the closing Waiting entry above. That entry exercises the rule on the work itself.
4. **Piece B:** a router fixture case through the existing eval harness. The ticket is Done, the latest code review is Approve, a close-out came after it, and an audit comment links an open PR. The selector must pick `review`, not `retrospective-audit`. If the harness cannot express it, the builder says so and the first live audit with a note-bound find is the observation.
5. **Behavioural acceptance (the Done-when):** the first close-out after piece A merges whose review named an outside find. Its summary must show a Waiting entry committed before the merge, and no ticket unless it names break, block or safety. The trail's follow-on ratio (`scripts/follow-on-ratio.mjs`) is read over the following weeks. Completion is not demonstrated until that close-out exists, so the close-out of piece A names this check for the operator.

### Likeliest ways it breaks

1. **A route still files.** A sentence left on a parallel surface (kickoff, completion signals, the manual) keeps minting. Caught by witness 1(iii) across all rendered kinds, and by the search for docs.
2. **A note entry blocks the merge.** Close-out writes an entry whose first path maps to another area, or to an unmapped file, and the guard goes red. The gate's fallback names the right note, and close-out already re-establishes CI before merging, so the failure is loud and pre-merge. The cost is a slower close-out, not a bad landing.
3. **The byte budget and rebase churn.** `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and the budget test change in almost every merge.
4. **(B)** **The audit's notes PR loops or is judged against the wrong ask** on a Done ticket. This is why (a), (b) and (c) exist and witness 4 checks it.

### Budget

Prompt size is frozen. Replace wording; do not only add it.

* `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` must replace text in each route:
  * review's "close-out files it, after checking it does not already exist";
  * review's two ledger "routed follow-up ticket" clauses;
  * close-out's Outside bullet and Triage's opening sentence;
  * the audit's "file a follow-up ticket … that still matters".
* Target: each ceiling is net flat or lower. Where one must rise, raise it with LIN-4401 and its reason beside it and in `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES`, and log it in `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`.
* Re-measure after every rebase. The budget fixture renders the empty-context branch.

### Area notes that bind this work

From `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` (`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`, `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, `lib/periodicals.js`) and `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` (`lib/dispatch-leftover.js`, `lib/completion-signals.js`).

**Lessons:**

* Prompt size is frozen, and old reasons go to "Ceiling history".
* `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and the budget test change in almost every merge: rebase, then re-measure (LIN-4393).
* Shared words live in an import-free leaf (LIN-4376). This is D1's home.
* Prompt words do not hold a shape; hold it in code or a test (LIN-4369). This is why D7 rests on tests, not wording.
* A route or lead change moves the router snapshots, `meta-prompt.baseline.txt` and the routing ceiling (LIN-4369). This applies to piece B only.
* Close-out merges a Periodical's PR as for any task, with no merge rule of its own (LIN-4390). D5 reuses that path; (c) adds no merge rule, only what to skip on a Done ticket.

**Waiting** (Security Review, 10 Nov., on `lib/prompt-formatters.js`): close-out writes review-worded entries to main unreviewed, with no content boundary. This change widens that, because entries now land in other areas' notes too. It is context, not scope: the size of the move does not take it on. The Waiting entries are still shape-checked by the guard and read as context, not scope, by later stages.

**Recent constraints** (`git log --oneline -15` on the touched files): LIN-4414 (Lessons capped, one retirement per build, guard on `parseNote`), LIN-4390 (Periodical hand-off; close-out merges), LIN-4379/4380 (Periodical notes path), LIN-4374/4376 (one leaf, retype guard). All of these files changed since the ticket was filed. The surveys' route inventory was re-checked at `94893cc35` and holds. Survey open-0's "18 unmapped `lib/` files" is stale: every `lib/` file maps, with `other-features` as the `^lib/` catch-all.

### Landing and session fit

Two sessions, split at the A/B seam. Each lands and is verified on its own.

* **Piece A** (LinearViewer PR, then the one-sentence simple-dispatcher PR) is the pre-merge gate. It carries every route that drives the 1.4 per landing and the Done-when's close-out check.
* **Piece B** depends on A's `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`. It is the audit's notes PR, plus the routing, review and close-out sentences for a Done ticket. It moves the router baseline and needs its own eval witness.

One session doing both would lose track of the router-baseline and eval regeneration while the template budget is being re-measured across rebases. A **breakdown** makes the two subtasks, with B blocked by A.

This plan should get a second reader before it is built. It touches close-out's merge-time duties, changes routing, and needs more than one session.

needs multiple sessions

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4401 @ 94893cc35

(simple-dispatcher read at `a42456c6f`.)

**The rule the ticket names isn't the main source of tickets.** `LEFTOVER_RULE` (`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`) covers *leftovers*: "code shape, not a defect". Its "Outside the area: a follow-up only close-out files" is one route. A second route, with its own wording, files more: review's **Inside or Outside the Ticket's Scope** (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, review template) marks class siblings and every What-CI-Did-Not-Prove ledger item *outside*, which means "a different problem". Close-out's **Settle the Ledger** then says "Outside: file it as a follow-up", and that isn't `LEFTOVER_RULE`'s text. If you edit only `LEFTOVER_RULE`, it reads as done and the 1.4/landing hardly moves. "Everywhere Harbour states it" has to include the ledger and class-sibling routes.

**Two axes are mixed up.** "Outside" in LEFTOVER_RULE means outside the change's *area*. In the ledger it means outside the ticket's *bounded classes* (John's LIN-2825 ruling: scope is discharged by doing it or dropping it, never by filing). The new rule splits the outside set again by consequence (breaks / blocks / safety → ticket; else → note). Write that test once, as a new constant beside `LEFTOVER_RULE`, and render it in all three places (review marking, Settle the Ledger, Follow-up Triage). Otherwise there'll be three spellings, and `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js` already polices retyping. "Touches safety" also needs a definition there, or every reviewer draws the line differently.

**Timing moves.** Follow-up Triage runs after merge and Done. A note has to land on the PR branch *before* merge: close-out already writes review's note entries there, then re-establishes CI, and `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` runs in CI. So outside finds have to be decided before the merge, and a malformed entry can block the merge.

**No home in some cases.** Guard check 3 requires a Waiting entry's first cited path to map to the note's area, which correctly forces the find into the *other* area's note. But LV has unmapped `lib/` files (R19 in `docs/reviews/integration-surface-maturity-review-2026-11-10.md`: 18 fall through), and repos without notes exist (`RETIRES_NONE.noWaiting` already assumes this; Jira repos too). The rule needs a stated fallback. My engineering call: write it in the change's summary comment, and file a ticket only where the provider can.

**Convergence depends on the drain.** More outside finds become Waiting entries, and the only steady drain is LIN-4414's one-per-build retirement. That only touches areas the build *touched*, so notes for rarely-touched areas will grow. Say so outright.

**Mechanics:** prompt-size budgets, `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`, LV's `docs/areas/README.md` ("Close-out is the only one that files a follow-up"), and `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md`. SD's README only points at the constant.

**Retires:** the "every outside find → ticket" line in close-out's ledger and triage text.

**What I'd do first:** list every prompt sentence that leads to filing (grep `file`/`follow-up` across `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and `lib/dispatch-leftover.js`) and tag each one leftover or ledger. Then add the single consequence constant, before changing any wording. "Done when the next close-out writes a note" can only be checked after merge, so name the first eligible close-out as the check.

## Survey global: LIN-4401 @ 94893cc35

*simple-dispatcher read at `a42456c6f`.*

**Where it lands.** In the stage words: `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`, review and close-out in `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, `leftoverPrompt` in `lib/dispatch-leftover.js`, and the two `docs/areas/README.md` copies. The area-notes system is four days old (LIN-4371 to LIN-4414) and still getting better: each step pulled wording into one leaf constant, guarded by `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js` and `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`. simple-dispatcher's README points at the constant, so only its "only close-out files" lines change there.

**The ticket is aimed at one of three spigots.** `LEFTOVER_RULE`'s "Outside the area: a follow-up only close-out files" is the one the ask names. There are two more:
1. Review's **Inside or Outside the Ticket's Scope** paragraph says "close-out files it", and close-out's **Settle the Ledger** has the bullet "**Outside**: file it as a follow-up". This wording is separate from the constant, and its "outside" means outside the ticket's bounded classes (LIN-2825), not outside the change's area. These items are often defects.
2. `retrospective-audit` files "a follow-up ticket ... for each finding that still matters" (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, `lib/completion-signals.js`). It runs after merge, with no branch, so it has nowhere to write a note.

Change only the constant, the obvious edit, and the ledger and audit routes keep filing. That leaves the rule spelled two ways, and probably most of the 1.4-per-landing rate untouched.

**Timing is the structural catch.** Close-out writes notes in **Make the Fixes**, before the merge. Filing happens in **Follow-up Triage**, after merge and Done. An outside find that becomes a note has to move from the later step to the earlier one, with its destination area named by review. The Workflow lines 2 and 5 and the `close-out` completion signals both say "file the outside follow-ups" and need to follow.

**The homeless finds.** `areas.json` maps all of `lib/` (`other-features` is a `^lib/` catch-all). It maps nothing under `tests/`, `scripts/`, `docs/` or `.github/`. The guard requires a Waiting entry's first path to map to its area, so a find in a test or CI file has no note to go to. Without a fallback it quietly goes back to being a ticket. The cheap rule: use the area of the code it concerns, else the summary comment.

**What leaves it better, within this task.** Add one `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` beside `LEFTOVER_RULE` that defines breaks, blocks and safety. Safety needs a concrete list: auth, secrets, data loss, irreversible writes.
